An implementation roadmap would have been developed that outlines short-term actions like launching a DER management platform pilot and initiating NWA feasibility studies, medium-term strategies for scaling successful pilots and formalizing support frameworks, and a long- term vision for a fully integrated DER-rich grid. The business model plan is pivotal in transitioning to a DER-rich energy landscape, promising to enhance grid reliability, flexibility, sustainability, and create new revenue streams and business opportunities for utilities. 6.1.5 Task 5: Analyze Scalability and National Replication Potential As operator of the NASEO-NARUC GEB Working Group, NASEO engaged State Energy Offices, Public Utility Commissions, and pertinent demand flexibility stakeholders on demand flexibility opportunities and impediments. This included holding a NASEO annual meeting plenary session on October 18, 2023, in Portland, Oregon on dynamic loads, virtual power plants, and connected communities’ session that featured speakers from U.S. DOE, New Jersey Board of Public Utilities, California Energy Commission, and Google discussing demand flexibility, Connected Communities, and related topics. NASEO staff also participated in a NASEO-NARUC State Microgrids Working Group workshop in Bethesda, Maryland on October 3-4, 2023, which included a tour of the Brookville Smart Energy Bus Depot microgrid, an integrated electric bus charging infrastructure project in Montgomery County, Maryland. Demand flexibility and grid-interactive aspects were included in site visit and workshop discussions and individual discussions with state officials. On November 3, 2023, NASEO attended virtually the CalFlexHub Symposium on November 3, 2023, and on December 15, 2023, spoke with EPA ENERGY STAR staff on the program’s Connected Criteria work. NASEO held other meetings and identified other resources pertinent 14 to demand flexibility, grid-interactive functionality, and DER integration. While most of these activities were held under separate project funding, they helped inform NASEO, the states, and this project on demand flexibility and associated opportunities and impediments to deployment and scalability and replication potential for demand flexibility, Connected Community, and related grid-edge solutions. The learnings from these national forums served as inputs and details were included in the baseline scalability study that was completed in budget period 1. They represent detailed inputs for policy, regulatory, and market research from existing programs and strategic direction setting happening across the country. 6.1.6 Task 6: Data Coordination PacifiCorp initiated monthly meetings for the data workstream portion of the UDERMS project to push the work forward as needed in this task. Project stakeholders met on a monthly basis or more frequently to discuss data related topics, conducted collaboration sessions, support project solutioning, and get updates on task and deliverable status. The work on this task was also directly related to the work performed for Subtask 1.2.0 as PacifiCorp and the project team reviewed and evaluated AMI meter data, deployment status of AMI metering at the participating facilities, evaluation of OCPP data, and analysis of available BESS data. The data coordination task was focused on data collection, data governance, data management, evaluation plan, and the intellectual property plan.
